newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, July up on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, July up on tight supply.

text.p: Concerns over the availability of soybeans for immediate shipment boosted CBOT July soybeans to sharp closing gains, and other months were mostly lower.
"Overnight registrations dropped down to virtually zip, suggesting that we still have very tight supplies" said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter.
Wednesday's deliverable stocks from the CBOT showed the supply of soybeans dropped 580,000 bushels to a scant 20,000.
One of the large commerical firms was said to have loaded the soybeans onto five barges at a Lake Michigan port, floor sources said.
Strength in cash markets was also cited as a reason for the rally in July. Traders said that soybeans traded in cash markets as much as 20 cents a bushel higher than on Wednesday.
"The processors have been picking up their bids and are looking for supplies," Gidel said.
New crop contracts traded higher for most of the session, but a late sell-off in wheat dragged the market lower near the close.
CBOT July soybeans settled up 11 cents per bushel at $8.41-1/2. August settled 2-1/2 cents higher at $7.84-1/2 while other months ended 3-1/2 to 1/2 cent lower.
Supply and demand data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture was initially seen as bearish for soybeans, but traders ignored the data after a short time.
"The report might have been a little bearish, but the main thing is we have really tight supplies," said one trader for a commercial firm.
In the report, USDA raised old crop ending stocks by five million bushels to 125 million and doubled soybean imports from 10 million to 20 million.
Cash traders were looking for the National Oilseed Processors Association to show a weekly crushing pace that ranged from 24.60 to 25.60 million bushels.
On the day, ABN-Amro Chicago Corp bought five million bushels July, Refco bought five million July and Rosenthal Collins bought 2.5 million November and two million July, traders said.
In options trade, Cargill bought 400 August $8.25 calls and Prudential Securities bought 400 July $8.00 puts. Lind-Waldock bought 500 July $8.50 calls.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 60,000 contracts. That figure compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 54,217, according to CBOT data.
